title: Audit logs: emit events for model rollout actions (canary toggles, pin/unpin) + legacy name mapping
author: Diego Santos
description: Summary: This instruments model rollout / deployment actions to emit schema-v1 audit events across the control plane and runtime rollout controller paths. Covered actions: canary enable/disable, pin/unpin model version, and fallback policy changes (including enabling/disabling automatic fallback). This also adds a backwards-compat mapping layer so customers consuming legacy event names continue to see equivalent events during the migration window. Motivation: Enterprise customers (and SOC2 evidence expectations) require complete, consistent audit logging for changes that materially impact availability/behavior of deployed models. Today rollout actions were only partially logged (and sometimes only as internal ops logs) with inconsistent naming and missing actor attribution. Changes: 1) New audit events (registered in audit-event registry) emitted from deployment-service for Console/API initiated rollouts and from runtime-rollout-controller for controller-initiated transitions. 2) Actor attribution rules: Console/API actions use end-user actor with propagated request_id; controller actions use service actor (runtime-rollout-controller) and include initiating change source when present (e.g., 'policy_engine' vs 'autoscaler'). 3) Target modeling: target.resource_type=model_deployment with deployment_id + model_id + variant_id; for pin/unpin we also include target.changes.before/after for pinned_model_version. 4) Outcome/error semantics: outcome=success|failure; failures include error.code and sanitized error.message (no secrets/prompt text). 5) Legacy mapping: emit legacy event names (config-gated) that map to the new canonical events; mapping is documented inline and covered by unit tests. Notes/compat: This does not change rollout behavior; only adds audit side effects. Event emission is synchronous with the rollout API handler but is non-blocking on exporter (enqueue + retry semantics handled downstream). If audit enqueue fails we still complete the rollout action, but we record metric audit_log.emit_failed and include a server-side warning log with request_id for correlation (per audit logging telemetry standard). Testing: Added unit tests for event payloads (required fields + redaction), and integration test coverage for canary toggles/pin operations. Related: Depends on schema/registry introduced in PRs #18421 and #18437; aligns with ENG-2485 and the sensitive action inventory for rollout actions. Follow-ups: Add coverage scanner expectations once sensitive-actions inventory file is updated, and verify Console UI field rendering for target.changes before/after.
commits: control-plane/deployments: emit audit events for rollout mutations (canary, pin/unpin, fallback policy)
runtime/rollout-controller: add audit hooks for controller-initiated canary transitions
audit/events: register rollout events + add legacy name mapping table
tests: add unit tests for payload schema + regression tests for legacy mapping
docs: developer notes on actor attribution for controller actions
implementation_notes: Event names added (schema v1): model.rollout.canary.enabled, model.rollout.canary.disabled, model.rollout.version.pinned, model.rollout.version.unpinned, model.rollout.fallback_policy.updated. Legacy mapping (dual-write, config flag AUDIT_LOG_LEGACY_EVENT_NAMES=true): model_rollout_canary_toggle -> model.rollout.canary.enabled|disabled (derived from payload), model_rollout_pin -> model.rollout.version.pinned, model_rollout_unpin -> model.rollout.version.unpinned, model_rollout_fallback_update -> model.rollout.fallback_policy.updated. Required fields enforced via helper: event_version=1, event_id (uuidv7), occurred_at (RFC3339), org_id, actor (type/user|service, id, display), request_id when available, ip/user_agent for user actions only, outcome, target, and redacted metadata. Payload redaction: do not include full routing policy blobs; include only policy_id and diff summary (keys changed) plus before/after of boolean flags and pinned version string.
review_conversation: Marcus Lin (Security): Can we confirm no prompt payload / headers are leaking into metadata? Also, for controller-initiated transitions, we still need a stable actor id and a way to link back to the initiating policy change if any.

Diego Santos (Author): Yep. Metadata is explicitly whitelisted; we only include deployment_id/model_id/variant_id, pinned_version, and a small fallback_policy diff (keys + before/after). No request headers or prompts. For controller path actor is actor.type=service actor.id=runtime-rollout-controller. I added optional metadata.initiating_event_id when the controller is acting as a follow-on to a rollout request (present in the internal message).

Nadia Rahman (Telemetry): Please make sure emit failures are visible. The description says non-blocking; we still need metrics that allow SRE to see drops vs delays. Are we using the shared emit wrapper that increments audit_log.emit_failed with service/event_name tags?

Diego Santos (Author): Updated to use audit.emitOrMetric() wrapper (same as API key work). Added service + event_name tags and request_id in warn log. The enqueue happens before returning but failures do not fail the API call.

Allison Grant (Observability): Naming: do we want model.rollout.* or deployments.rollout.*? Prior decision in naming guidelines was to keep user-visible resources, but model rollout lives under deployments domain. Also ensure target.resource_type matches schema enums.

Diego Santos (Author): Good call. Renamed to model.rollout.* to align with inventory wording from ENG-2485 and existing docs, but target.resource_type is model_deployment (enum) and includes model_id + deployment_id. I added a short comment in events/model_rollout.ts explaining the namespace choice and the mapping to model_deployment target.
Chloe Martin (Console): For canary toggles initiated via Console, do we have request_id propagation all the way into deployment-service? We had gaps in another service.

Diego Santos (Author): Yes. The console backend already sets x-redwood-request-id; deployment-service takes it into context and passes to audit emit. Added integration test asserting request_id present for console-initiated canary enable.

Marcus Lin (Security) - Requested changes: Add unit test asserting ip/user_agent are absent for actor.type=service and present for actor.type=user (where available). Also ensure legacy mapping doesn't accidentally double-emit in environments that already dual-write elsewhere.

Diego Santos (Author): Added tests for ip/user_agent behavior and a guard: legacy dual-write is only applied at the emitting service boundary (deployment-service + controller). Registry mapping is pure (no side effects) and behind a single config toggle checked in one place.
Marcus Lin (Security): Looks good now. Approved.
Nadia Rahman (Telemetry): Approved after wrapper + metrics.
release_notes: Audit logs now include model rollout actions (canary enable/disable, pin/unpin model version, fallback policy changes). Legacy audit event names are emitted in parallel (configurable) during migration.
